text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mention a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; have you noticed any specific pattern to the rash, such as a "sandpaper" texture or a rash that appears in waves?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Scarlet fever (Group A Streptococcal pharyngitis with toxin-mediated rash).

The patient is a child with a 1-day lag between prodromal symptoms (fever, rhinorrhea) and a facial rash sparing the perioral area, which is highly characteristic of scarlet fever. Have you noticed "sandpaper" texture to the rash or a "pastia" sign (red streaks in skin folds)? REQUEST TEST: Rapid_strep_A_test
